brief.scope: Independently review GPT-6's first lane-policy contract/data slice against the owner scope and adjudicated ruling. Limit to the three changed files and necessary owning seams. Check implementable authority/ref/digest binding, profile/role/harness separation, exact effective grants, maintenance without self-authorization, startup/bootstrap and old records, complete settle/resume/collect/land/ladder coverage, actual dependency boundaries and truthful containment. Product writes must pass only in the proper profile; shared inspection and dev tooling must remain usable without the Symfony app/vendor. Missing metadata cannot widen grants. Check third-profile cases, exact refusal order/shapes and independent-test readiness. No runtime implementation demanded in this inert contract slice; no broad audit. Return concise approve/changes with reproducible material gaps and smallest corrections. Read-only: no source/tests/settings/host/DB/network edits or vendor launches.

findings.claim: The protected set omits the gate and authorization sources the contract itself calls mandatory, and every one of them sits inside `dev`'s sole write root `ops/`. lane-policy.md:288 requires `ops/bin/suites.sh` "including existing laneconf closure, literal and instrument-conformance gates" and :275 says "Existing suite/conformance gates remain mandatory for executable delivery", yet `ops/bin/suites.sh`, `ops/conductor/tools/laneconf.py`, `ops/bin/dispatch.sh`, `ops/bin/go.sh`, all of `ops/devlane/hooks/`, `ops/conductor/tools/decisions.py` and `ops/conductor/decisions.seed.json` appear nowhere in protected_authority_paths. Under :95 ("Protected paths cannot be edited by routine profile membership alone") the converse holds: an ordinary `dev` job, with no maintenance record and no owner decision, may delete the suite entrypoint, the closure/literals gates, the hooks, and the tracked seed export the decisions register names as its restore source (ops/conductor/tools/decisions.py:138) — while the same job is blocked from `ops/README.md`. The list protects five consumer modules (launch.py, record.py, land.py, ladder.py, isolation.py) and leaves the enforcement levers and the decision-store restore path open, so the declared gate-source discipline at :106-107 has no data behind it. Smallest correction: add `ops/bin/`, `ops/devlane/hooks/`, `ops/conductor/tools/laneconf.py`, `ops/conductor/tools/decisions.py` and `ops/conductor/decisions.seed.json` to protected_authority_paths, and state the inclusion rule (every gate entrypoint, conformance module and authorization store is protected) so the list is derivable rather than enumerated by hand.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '5,15p;16,18p' ops/lane-policy.json; sed -n '95p;275p;288p' ops/conductor/lane-policy.md; git ls-files ops/bin ops/devlane/hooks; grep -c 'suites.sh' ops/lane-policy.json; grep -n 'seed the store' ops/conductor/tools/decisions.py

findings.claim: `shared_read_roots` is a mandatory key with no semantics anywhere in the change. It appears exactly twice: once as data (`["AGENTS.md","CLAUDE.md","docs/","ops/"]`) and once in the key list at :52. No rule defines what it permits or forbids, no refusal class references it, the effective-grants section (:117-154) covers only writes and dependency edges, and no prescribed case exercises it. Worse, the only reading that would make it load-bearing contradicts the contract: as a read ceiling it excludes `src/` and `packages/`, so :40-41 ("Both lanes may read shared contracts and inspect or describe application source") and case P1 (":293, `dev` ... describes Symfony: pass") would refuse, and `prod` could not read its own `src/`. An independent implementer must either enforce it and break P1/P2 or ignore a key the contract declares required. Smallest correction: either define the key as an additive cross-profile read allowance that never narrows profile reads, with a prescribed case, or drop it from the schema and from the data.

The protected-path rule is stated three times with two incompatible meanings, so the `authority_maintenance` boolean's effect is undetermined. The profile table at :29 grants `dev` "`ops/`, excluding protected authority unless separately authorized" — authorization alone, no profile condition. The grants formula at :129 subtracts "protected paths lacking the maintenance authorization" — again no profile condition. But :95-96 reads "A profile with `authority_maintenance: true` may propose edits only when the trusted caller also supplies ... record", which is a necessary condition for true-valued profiles and says nothing about false-valued ones. Under the loose reading a `dev` job plus a valid maintenance record may edit `ops/README.md` and the boolean is decorative; under the strict reading it refuses `lane-write`. No prescribed case decides it: P4 (:296) exercises only the `authority-maintenance` profile, and there is no negative case for false-profile-plus-record. An independent test author cannot write that test. Smallest correction: state at :95 that `authority_maintenance: false` refuses every protected path regardless of any supplied record, restate :29 and :129 in those terms, and add a negative case "`dev` with a valid maintenance record editing `ops/README.md`: `lane-write`".

The admission record is the single root of trust and has no named store, format or field set. :76-78 says the owner admits ref and digest "through the existing conductor decision/custody record" without naming it; the repository holds three candidates (`ops/conductor/decisions-register.md` with its host store `~/.local/state/agentscient/decisions.db`, `ops/conductor/decisions.seed.json`, `ops/conductor/handwork-ledger.md`) and the contract picks none. `brief.policy.admission` at :159-161 is `(record, sha256)` with no statement of what `record` references, what it must contain, or how a consumer verifies it "outside worker control" (:99). The register the phrase most likely points at is itself standing PROPOSED (ops/conductor/decisions-register.md:3). Consequence: P4's positive half ("plus existing trusted authorization", :296) cannot be constructed by the independent test author this slice is written for, and the whole authority chain at :75-104 is unimplementable as written. Smallest correction: name the store and verb (e.g. `ops/conductor/tools/decisions.py show <id>` against the host store), give the admission record's required fields (id, path, ref, blob sha256, decided_by owner, evidence), and state that the store is outside every profile's repository write roots.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '76,78p;99p;159,161p;296p' ops/conductor/lane-policy.md; ls ops/conductor/decisions-register.md ops/conductor/decisions.seed.json ops/conductor/handwork-ledger.md; sed -n '1,8p;17,20p' ops/conductor/decisions-register.md

findings.claim: The two rules for what authorizes protected maintenance are mutually exclusive. :96-98 requires "an existing owner-authorized maintenance record identifying the principal, admitted policy ref/digest, exact bounded paths, purpose and job/lineage" — fields that only a per-dispatch artifact can carry, since job/lineage and the admitted ref/digest are not knowable when a standing instruction is written. :103-104 then says "An existing applicable owner instruction suffices; do not invent a fresh approval ritual for already authorized maintenance" — the owner's requirement of no permission questions for ordinary authorized work. A standing owner instruction cannot satisfy the :97-98 field list, so exactly one of the two sentences is operative and the contract does not say which. This is the seam the owner brief singled out ("Explain how policy/instruction maintenance is authorized under the existing trusted policy without candidate self-authorization"), and P4's phrase "existing trusted authorization" inherits the ambiguity. Smallest correction: split the two forms explicitly — a standing owner instruction admitted once as a maintenance grant covering named path prefixes, versus a per-job record for paths outside any standing grant — and say which fields each requires.

The permitted value set for `standing` is unstated. :54-55 says only "`standing` is `proposal` (descriptive, never an activation switch)", which reads as a fixed required literal, while :60 refuses "unknown keys, wrong types" without covering out-of-set values. An activated policy would have to keep saying `proposal` or change this contract, and no prescribed case fixes either the accepted set or the refusal for a bad value. Smallest correction: enumerate the allowed values (e.g. `proposal`, `active`) and add one negative case for an unknown value refusing `lane-policy`.

The `allow_declared_outputs: false` branch is never exercised by any prescribed case. :131-132 says external-output writes "are empty when the profile's `allow_declared_outputs` is false", but all three shipped profiles set it true (ops/lane-policy.json:26,37,51), P3 (:295) sets "both booleans false" on the fixture profile yet prescribes only the repository-write results (`unittest/example.txt` passes, `src/Example.php` refuses), and N6 (:302) tests only the missing-declaration path with an implied true. The independent test author has no case telling them that a present, valid output declaration must still yield no grant under a false-valued profile. Smallest correction: extend P3's prescribed result to state that a declared external `out/` write refuses `lane-write` under that fixture profile.

The landed commit message is corrupted relative to the producer's envelope. The code record's `envelope.commit.body` (in/20260906T021901Z-code-codex-444175.json:223) has the two-line sentence "Validation: git diff --check; strict JSON parsing, changed links and static / example consistency checked by a disposable script outside the source tree." Because the first wrapped line matches `Token: value`, trailer handling hoisted it into the trailer block below `Source: owner 2026-09-05`, leaving its continuation "example consistency checked by a disposable script outside the source tree." stranded in the body as a sentence fragment. The landed "Validation:" trailer therefore ends mid-clause and states a truncated claim about what was checked. The `Source:` and `Co-Authored-By: gpt-6-astra <noreply@openai.com>` trailers are otherwise correct and the actual-model naming is right. Smallest correction: reflow the body so no wrapped prose line begins with a trailer-shaped token, or make Validation a single-line trailer.

artifacts.REVIEW:
REVIEW of 9ca4727237ba036885eebcce50156f617a411f17 against c06ed9442ba51c9e96aa8de9f9bde93d0843a6cc. Artifact: GPT-6's first lane-policy contract/data slice, three files (ops/conductor/lane-policy.md +325, ops/lane-policy.json +54, ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md +36). This reviewer produced none of them. Inputs read whole from in/. Verdict: changes.

WHAT HOLDS. Scope is exactly the three authorized files; no executable source, tests, lane.conf key, executor, jobs schema, hook or MCP action was added. The ruling's essential corrections are present and correctly stated: authority is the fixed tracked path plus admitted git ref and blob digest, with laneconf.get/LANE_CONF/LANE_POLICY_PATH/lane.local.conf/environment explicitly excluded (lane-policy.md:75-86) — I confirmed laneconf.py:140 resolves LANE_CONF and values()/get() at 187-197 overlay the environment ahead of the file, so the rejection is well founded. Launch/task ownership with policy as one intersection term, and absence contributing the empty set rather than profile roots, is explicit (:120-135). All six refusal classes are declared with wire-conformant shape (:214-223); the one worked example matches docs/wire.md's expected/found/needed line. Containment honesty is accurate: I confirmed launch.py:379-382 sets containment "os" only for codex and "policy" for claude/grok, and CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS at :442 carries no Write/Edit, matching :230-235. The residual claim is measured-true: _residual_entries exists at launch.py:1614, uses `status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall` and a separate `ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z` at :1646-1650, handles R/C endpoints at :1635-1641, and filters only _is_cache_residual — so "`git status -uall` alone does not see ignored files" (:186-187) is correct. The acceptance holes the ruling named are covered: land.py:203-227 accepts envelope-not-ok when collected and ladder.py:717 accepts closed+ok, and the transition table at :177-183 plus N5 forbid worker verdict, exit 0 and collect-verify from accepting. brief.policy/result.policy nest cleanly under record.py's FIELDS projection (record.py:11-15,39) without touching the field list. Profile separation is right: no profile carries both product and tooling write roots, prod cannot write ops/, dev cannot write product roots, and dependency-installation is explicitly not a profile grant (:37-38). Bootstrap is honest — the slice lands under existing owner authorization, its own record is declared unbound, old records keep bytes without backfill (:238-270). All ten changed links resolve, including the #collect and #the-refusal-wire anchors and both .dev/ladder-inputs owner briefs; every protected path exists in the tree except ops/conductor/tools/lane_policy.py, which is the intended future evaluator.

WHAT MUST CHANGE. One P1: the protected set (lane-policy.json:5-15) omits the gate levers and authorization stores the contract calls mandatory — ops/bin/suites.sh, ops/conductor/tools/laneconf.py, ops/bin/dispatch.sh, ops/bin/go.sh, ops/devlane/hooks/, ops/conductor/tools/decisions.py, ops/conductor/decisions.seed.json — all of which lie inside dev's sole write root, so an ordinary dev job may delete the enforcement gates and the decision-store restore seed with no authorization while being refused ops/README.md. Four P2: shared_read_roots is a required key with no semantics whose only load-bearing reading contradicts case P1 and prod's own src/ reads; the protected-path rule is stated three times with two incompatible meanings, leaving authority_maintenance:false-plus-record undetermined and untested; the admission record that anchors the whole trust chain has no named store, format or fields, so P4's positive case is unbuildable; and the two rules for what authorizes maintenance (a per-job record carrying job/lineage versus an existing standing owner instruction) are mutually exclusive as written. Three P3: standing's permitted value set, the unexercised allow_declared_outputs:false branch, and a trailer-mangled commit message whose Validation line ends mid-clause.

ABSENCE DECLARED. I did not execute the JSON through a parser: python3 invocation was refused by this session's sandbox. Structure was verified by whole-file inspection — five top-level keys matching the declared set, three profiles each with exactly the four declared subkeys, no duplicate keys, no repeated entries in any root list — but strict-parse confirmation is inspection, not measurement. No suites were run and no runtime enforcement was exercised or claimed; none is demanded by this inert slice. No source, tests, settings, host, database or network changes; no vendor launch.
